summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted after a mechanical fall resulting in epistaxis and right knee pain. She landed face-first and on her right knee, causing a nasal bleed controlled with anterior-posterior packing and a vertically oriented, minimally displaced patellar fracture identified on CT. Arthrocentesis removed 110cc of blood from a large suprapatellar effusion, and the knee was immobilized in a brace for non-operative management. Her platelet count, previously 10,000 during a recent admission for AVNRT-related syncope, was 103,000 on admission but downtrended to 67,000; aspirin was held and heparin initiated for DVT prophylaxis per hematologist guidance. The nasal tampon was removed without rebleeding. She remained stable with no arrhythmias, and her chronic diastolic heart failure was managed with continued medications. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehab with orthopedic follow-up in two weeks, ongoing platelet monitoring, and cardiology follow-up for pending EP evaluation.
